q: A store has 25% off everything. The discount on a backpack is $9. Rosa buys the backpack at the sale price and pays with a $40 bill. How much change does Rosa get?
key: Answer: C. $9 is 25% (one fourth) of the regular price, so the regular price is 4 × $9 = $36. Sale price: $36 − $9 = $27. Change: $40 − $27 = $13. $31 takes only the discount from $40. $4 uses the regular price. $9 stops at the discount.

q: Which expression is equivalent to 400 − 8 × (30 − 4)?
key: Answer: D. 8 × (30 − 4) = 8 × 30 − 8 × 4 = 240 − 32 = 208, and 400 − 208 = 192. Taking away the whole group flips the inside minus to a plus: 400 − 240 + 32 = 192. The second choice keeps the minus (it gives 128).

topic: Finding Area/Perimeter of Rectangle, given Length & Width
q: The width of a rectangle is the length divided by 3. The perimeter of the rectangle is 48 feet. What is the area of the rectangle?
key: Answer: C. Length = 3 widths. Perimeter = width + 3 widths + width + 3 widths = 8 widths = 48, so the width is 6 and the length is 18. Area = 18 × 6 = 108. 144 treats it as a 12 by 12 square. 36 is 6 × 6.

q: The tick marks on the number line are evenly spaced. D is the midpoint between C and another point, E. What is the value of E?

q:
Sam cut three pieces of rope.
Rope 1: 2 yards, 2 feet, 5 inches
Rope 2: 3 yards, 1 inch
Rope 3: 1 yard, 5 feet, 5 inches
Which statement is true? (1 yard = 3 feet; 1 foot = 12 inches)

choices.D: Rope 1 and Rope 3 are the same length.

key: Answer: D. Change each to inches. Rope 1: 72 + 24 + 5 = 101. Rope 2: 108 + 1 = 109. Rope 3: 36 + 60 + 5 = 101. Ropes 1 and 3 are both 101 inches. Rope 3 looks shorter only because it has 1 yard, but its 5 feet make up for it.

q: Which shape ALWAYS has two pairs of parallel sides and four sides of equal length, but does NOT always have four right angles?
key: Answer: D. Check all three conditions. A rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides and 4 equal sides, and its angles do not have to be right angles. A square always has right angles. A rectangle does not always have 4 equal sides. A trapezoid has only one pair of parallel sides.

q: The volume of a rectangular prism is 60 cubic inches. Its height is 5 inches. Which equation can be used to find the length, l, of the prism? (V = l × w × h)
key: Answer: D. 60 = l × w × 5. Divide both sides by 5: 12 = l × w. Then l = 12 ÷ w. 55 subtracts the height instead of dividing. 300 multiplies by the height.

q: In a sequence, each number is 8 more than the number before it. The 7th number in the sequence is 61. What is the 22nd number in the sequence?
key: Answer: B. From the 7th number to the 22nd number is 22 − 7 = 15 jumps. 15 × 8 = 120. 61 + 120 = 181. 173 uses 14 jumps, 189 uses 16 jumps, and 237 uses 22 jumps (counting from the start instead of from the 7th).

q: A shop had 300 bracelets. On Saturday, 40% of the bracelets were sold. Of the bracelets that were NOT sold, 13 were blue. How many of the unsold bracelets were blue?

q: A library cart had 96 books. In the morning, 14 of the books were put on the shelves. In the afternoon, 13 of the books still on the cart were put on the shelves. Then 10 new books were added to the cart. How many books are on the cart now?
key: Answer: C. Morning: 1/4 of 96 = 24, so 72 are left. Afternoon: 1/3 of 72 = 24, so 48 are left. Add 10: 58. 48 forgets the 10 new books. 50 takes 1/3 of all 96 instead of the 72 left.

q: A jar has red, blue, and green beads. There are 4 times as many red beads as blue beads. There are 2 times as many blue beads as green beads. There are 66 beads in all. How many red beads are in the jar?
key: Answer: D. Use parts. Green = 1 part. Blue = 2 times green = 2 parts. Red = 4 times blue = 8 parts. In all: 1 + 2 + 8 = 11 parts = 66, so 1 part = 6. Red = 8 × 6 = 48. 12 is blue and 6 is green (stopping one step early). 33 just halves 66.

q: Which expression means “4 less than 3 times the sum of n and 5”?
key: Answer: A. Read from the inside: “the sum of n and 5” is (n + 5), and it needs brackets because the 3 multiplies the whole sum. “3 times” it: 3 × (n + 5). “4 less than” that: take 4 away at the END. Without brackets, the 3 multiplies only n. “4 less than” does not mean 4 minus.
